sources.title: Civilization and Floods in the Indus Valley
sources.access_depth: Full publisher-hosted primary field account read; HTML acquired
sources.locator: Paragraphs beginning One of the first objectives and A boring rig; boring-rig caption
sources.observation: Bore material included brick, sherds, bangles and ash to 39 ft below contemporary plain; groundwater about 15 ft below plain.

sources.authors: Richard H. Meadow and Jonathan Mark Kenoyer
sources.title: Excavations at Harappa 1994–1995: New Perspectives on the Indus Script, Craft Activities, and City Organization
sources.access_depth: Full published chapter PDF acquired; title and conclusion read
sources.observation: Railway roadbed rubble removal contributed to destruction, especially Period 3C/later deposits; ancient Harappans also reused baked bricks.
sources.limits: Do not assign every missing brick wall to nineteenth-century railway work. Exact 1856 date not verified from this passage.

sources.authors: W.D. Page, J.N. Alt, L.S. Cluff and George Plafker
sources.title: Evidence for the recurrence of large-magnitude earthquakes along the Makran coast of Iran and Pakistan
sources.access_depth: Full primary abstract at USGS institutional record read and acquired; journal full text not obtained
sources.locator: USGS record https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70012441 , Abstract first two sentences
sources.observation: Raised beaches/terraces indicate episodic uplift; 1945 earthquake produced 1–3 m measured uplift at Pasni/Ormara.
sources.limits: Abstract evidence only. Pasni is local to P21; Ormara lies east of P21. Event displacement is not a Bronze Age shoreline reconstruction or constant rate.

sources.authors: Raphaël Normand, Guy Simpson and Abbas Bahroudi
sources.title: Pleistocene Coastal Evolution in the Makran Subduction Zone
sources.access_depth: Full publisher article HTML acquired; abstract, introduction and geological-setting sections read
sources.locator: Abstract; Geological Setting; Geology at the Coastal Makran, final regional uplift discussion
sources.observation: Regional uplift interacts with erosion and sediment transport; local normal faults coexist with general uplift.
sources.limits: Study field area is southeast Iran; Pleistocene terrace ages/rates cannot be assigned to Bronze Age Pakistani P21.

sources.title: A Search for Ancient Seaports
sources.access_depth: Full publisher-hosted primary field narrative read; HTML acquired
sources.locator: Sutkagen-dor discussion; Sotka-koh paragraphs following Burned Hill; paragraph Three natural forces
sources.observation: Sutkagen-dor was 35 miles inland in the account and Sotka-koh 9 miles north of Pasni. Continuing uplift, river alluvium and beach deposition altered both settings. The nearer ancient coast/tidal access is an interpretation.
sources.limits: No dated local Bronze Age shoreline section supplied. Dales says Sotka-koh could not have stood directly on sea coast; port/contact role remains a hypothesis.

sources.authors: District Administration Jammu, Government of India
sources.title: Akhnoor Fort
sources.access_depth: Full official district heritage page read; HTML acquired
sources.locator: Paragraph This two-storeyed fort; paragraph This fort, where excavation; final Manda sentence
sources.observation: Akhnoor Fort stands on an ancient site with Harappan pottery, early historic pottery and Kushana remains; page places Manda inside the fort.
sources.limits: Undated heritage summary, not an excavation report. Its continuing-excavation wording does not verify a 2026 season. No particular river trade, frontier extent or urban size established.

sources.title: Shortugaï
sources.access_depth: Full primary mission institutional site account read; HTML acquired; 1978/1989 excavation reports not fully read
sources.locator: First three paragraphs; Bibliographie sur Shortugaï
sources.observation: Survey 1975, tests 1976, excavations 1977–79; four periods include Mature Harappan and later cultural phases. Account gives 2.5 ha, 993 m² opened and about 90,000 sherds.
sources.limits: Area is a mission summary, not phase-specific. Sherd count has no supplied volume/density calibration. Valley site is not cave/high-mountain proof.

sources.authors: S. Kathiroli, S. Badrinarayanan, D.V. Rao, B. Sasisekaran and K.M. Sivakolundu
sources.title: New Archaeological sites in the Gulf of Cambay, India
sources.access_depth: Full three-page primary article acquired from Semantic Scholar mirror and read; DOI landing page failed
sources.locator: Printed pp. 16–18 / PDF pp. 1–3; Geological setting, sample paragraph, Chronology
sources.observation: NIOT used sonar, grab/dredge and gravity/vibro cores. Article reports terrestrial facies and dated carbonized wood about 9544–9545 cal BP; authors infer habitation.
sources.limits: Cores cannot be omitted from the account. Secure association between dated wood, objects and specific built features is not demonstrated in this brief report. Context criticism is reviewer inference; primary discussion/reply not read.
